uncited: It serves as the foundational statistical method for the Karhunen-Loeve Transform (KLT) [Parent], providing the eigenvectors used to decorrelate volume data, and is distinct from its sibling [KLT Decompression with VQ](5374-klt-decompression-with-vq.md) by focusing on the basis computation rather than the quantization scheme.
**Inputs:** A set of $N$ input vectors $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^N$, where each $X_i \in \mathbb{R}^D$.
**Compute Covariance Matrix:** Calculate the covariance matrix $C$ of the sample points $X_i$.
**Select Principal Directions:** Select the top $d$ eigenvectors $\hat{u}_j$ corresponding to the largest eigenvalues $\lambda_j$.
Typical values depend on the compression ratio required.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the covariance matrix ($D \times D$) or the full SVD components.
*   **When to use:** When data exhibits strong linear correlations and computational resources allow for SVD/eigendecomposition.
*   **When not to use:** When data has complex nonlinear manifolds or when real-time performance is critical and $D$ is very large.
PCA was introduced as a method for dimensionality reduction in information visualization and other fields.
It is closely related to the Karhunen-Loeve Transform (KLT) [Parent].
